Introduction and meaning
Disturbing religious assembly. BNS restatement of IPC 296. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 296. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 300 is the rule on “Disturbing religious assembly”. The section provides that . Whoever voluntarily causes disturbance to any assembly lawfully engaged in the performance of religious worship, or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 300 exists so that “Disturbing religious assembly” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVI — Of Offences Relating to Religion. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Defiling a place of worship, outraging religious feelings, disturbing an assembly.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 300 (Disturbing religious assembly) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 300 (Disturbing religious assembly), Chapter XVI — Of Offences Relating to Religion.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) . Whoever voluntarily causes disturbance to any assembly lawfully engaged in the performance of religious worship, or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 300 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 300 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Defiling a place of worship, outraging religious feelings, disturbing an assembly.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Analytical comment. Explain a condition, a proviso, or a practical difficulty in applying s. 300. Do not invent case names.
